topic: How Multilayer Perceptrons (MLP) Store Facts in Transformers
target_audience: University students with a basic background in linear algebra and neural networks.

sections.title: The Analogy: From Books to Weights
lecture_lines: Transformers act as advanced knowledge engines.

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Linear Transformation Concept
lecture_lines: Linear transformations map vectors between spaces.

sections.title: Key-Value Memories: The MLP Mechanism
lecture_lines: MLPs contain a Key layer for patterns.
The Value layer stores factual vectors.
This mechanism enables rapid fact recall.
animations: Display the search query vector moving toward the Key layer. (Color #FF6600)
Show the Value layer containing stored vectors. (Color #00FFCC)
Highlight the matching process between query and key. (Color #FFFFFF)
Display a 'fire' animation on the triggered key neuron. (Color #FFFF00)
Extract and animate the factual vector from the Value layer. (Color #FF00FF)

sections.title: Encoding Facts: The Weight Update
lecture_lines: Facts are distributed across neural weights.
Learning shifts dials in the machine.
Weights map inputs to factual regions.
animations: Display weight matrix grid highlighting changed cells. (Color #FF6600)

sections.title: Synthesis and Summary
lecture_lines: MLPs serve as dynamic memory banks.
Knowledge is embedded in network structure.
This enables flexible generalization and reasoning.
